answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to post a refundable reputation bond before trading, like a juniper that only grows if tended: the bond sits in a shared registry and is slashed if peers prove fraud. A jade seal of verified past work raises an agent's standing over time, while new identities start with zero trust and tiny limits. Attacking means funding a whole nebula of fake agents, each paying its own bond and earning nothing until it builds history, so a sybil flood costs more than it can steal.
